items.description: "A LoadBalancer Service with no ready endpoints, or no MetalLB `ServiceL2Status` (the DHCP failure itself)" raises a critical alert on every LoadBalancer Service except KubeCoder environments' (Ruling D3), which the rule recognises by the `app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: kubecoder` label. On the outage's chain (pod not Ready, so the EndpointSlice is not ready, so MetalLB withdraws and no ServiceL2Status exists; handover report.md) the alert fires. A stopped KubeCoder environment raises no alert, and a LoadBalancer Service in a KubeCoder namespace that lacks the label stays in scope. A gap in MetalLB's own metrics does not read as every Service unannounced. Evidence at planning: `metallb_speaker_announced` carries one series per announced Service as `service="<ns>/<name>"`. On 2026-10-03, 42 of 65 LoadBalancer Services were unannounced, all labelled environments in kubecoder-prd/kubecoder-dev. kube-state-metrics v2.20.0 ran with only `--port`/`--resources`, so no Service label was exported then.

"Whether DHCP answers at all: a DISCOVER from outside the pod network": a probe on srviac sends a relay-style DISCOVER to the DHCP service every few minutes and records the result through srviac's node-exporter. A critical alert fires when no OFFER comes back, and a warning fires when the result is stale or missing. The probe takes no lease. Evidence at planning: one DISCOVER from srviac with giaddr 10.1.0.45, sent from UDP 67, got an OFFER (10.1.1.80) after 3.018 s, from 10.1.0.29:85, and dnsmasq logged DHCPDISCOVER/DHCPOFFER for it (attachments/dhcp-probe.md).
items.owed_after: the operator's `ansible-playbook playbooks/site.yml --limit srviac`, which puts the probe on srviac

items.description: "OIDC discovery at auth.ginbov.nl failing" raises a critical alert. A blackbox exporter in the Prometheus deploy probes https://auth.ginbov.nl/realms/homelab/.well-known/openid-configuration. A probe that cannot run (exporter down, scrape failing) does not read as a passing probe.

"CrashLoopBackOff or ImagePullBackOff" raises an alert per Ruling D2: every namespace on the production cluster, severity warning, after the condition has held 15 minutes, one alert per pod. A crash loop's short running spells, and a pull flipping between ErrImagePull and ImagePullBackOff, do not restart the 15 minutes. Evidence at planning: kube-state-metrics v2.20.0 runs with only `--port`/`--resources`, and Prometheus history holds keycloak-prd ImagePullBackOff and dnsmasq-prd dhcp CrashLoopBackOff from 2026-09-25.
"a node NotReady" raises a critical alert, cluster-wide (Ruling D2). The window lets a node's ordinary reboot pass.

"an Argo app not Healthy. Slice 028 (ANS-118) covers Argo's sync-failed and degraded alerts; check the overlap." The overlap is checked, and no new Argo rule is added. ArgoCDSyncStillFailed and ArgoCDHealthStillDegraded (PrometheusDeploy config/prd/values.yaml:306, :336) and D7's events (routes at :422-426) cover sync-failed and degraded. The pod rule catches the outage's Keycloak image pull and DHCP crash loop.

"Whole-cluster loss ... an out-of-cluster heartbeat closes that", through healthchecks.io per Ruling D1. Prometheus raises an alert that always fires, and Alertmanager delivers it to the healthchecks.io ping URL through a webhook receiver, never more than 5 minutes apart. It never reaches Telegram, nothing else reaches the webhook, and it sends no "resolved" ping, so pings stop when Prometheus or Alertmanager stops. The ping URL comes from OpenBao kv/eso/prd/prometheus/prd/healthchecks (ping_url) through ESO and never appears in the repo or the rendered config.
When Alertmanager's pings stop, healthchecks.io notifies the operator over Telegram (Ruling F1).
items.owed_after: the operator's confirmation, after a drill that stops the pings past the check's period plus grace, that healthchecks.io's Telegram notification arrived

items.description: "create a read-only Elasticsearch user that can only read the `filebeat-*` indices, and store its credential in OpenBao", with the scope Ruling review-Q1 sets in place of "only read the `filebeat-*` indices": the user is read-only over all data and can log into Kibana. The Elasticsearch setup Job creates it. It reads every data index, through the Elasticsearch API and in Kibana (Discover), and it can write nothing, manage nothing in the cluster or its indices, and edit nothing in Kibana. Witnessed live under Ruling D4's single read of the password: a write is refused, and so is an administrative call. Its password is at OpenBao kv/eso/prd/elasticsearch/prd/filebeat-reader (password), reaches the Job through ESO, and appears in no repo. prd's ESO reads eso/prd/* (Ansible ansible/inventories/prd/group_vars/openbao.yml:99), so the KubeCoder card can read the same leaf. Evidence at planning: prd runs Elasticsearch 8.15.0 (its log, version[8.15.0]), whose built-in `viewer` role the ruling names as matching this shape.

"Then the Kibana route ANS-164 put in docs/runbooks/argocd.md for a replaced hook's log can be checked, and it becomes a real answer", confirmed through Kibana per Ruling review-Q1. Logged into Kibana with the new credential, the route returns a current Argo CD hook pod's lines. The equivalent API query the runbook gains returns the same pod's lines from Elasticsearch with the same credential. The test phase makes both, reading the password once under Ruling D4. A query sent to Elasticsearch directly does not stand in for the Kibana route. The runbook's route (docs/runbooks/argocd.md:156-177) then drops "unconfirmed" and no longer names tf-presync-fieldnotes-prd-sx956 as the check owed. It gives Kibana at the address where it answers, and reads as an answer for whoever holds the credential: a person in Kibana, an agent through ELASTIC_URL/ELASTIC_USER/ELASTIC_PASSWORD. The Ansible repo reaches origin only after both queries have returned the pod's lines. Evidence at planning: Kibana answers at http://kibana.home with its login form (/internal/security/login_state lists the basic provider), and https://kibana.home, which the route names today, lands on another service (witnessed 2026-10-03).

The Elasticsearch setup Job runs again on any change to its spec, not only on an image-pin change (today its name derives from the pin alone, ElasticsearchDeploy chart/templates/elasticsearch-setup-job.yaml:6). No Argo CD sync of elasticsearch-prd fails while the slice's two commits to that repo (the phase's and CI's pin) land.

Every alert this slice adds, except the heartbeat, reaches the Telegram receiver its severity picks (loud for critical, silent otherwise) and gets a "resolved". tests/alert-routing.py asserts that, and asserts the heartbeat as its one exception.

No coverage is lost: every existing rule group's promtool tests and the routing assertions still run and pass. Each new rule group has promtool tests with a firing and a quiet case at every edge it claims.
The srviac play that installs the DHCP probe reports changed=0 on a second run, and its --check --diff shows the first run's changes.
items.owed_after: the operator's `ansible-playbook playbooks/site.yml --limit srviac` (check mode, then apply, then a second apply)

items.description: healthchecks.io is modelled in the architecture artifact (Ruling review-A1). It is declared as an external service in the Architecture repo, the way Telegram's Bot API is (Architecture docs/architecture/external-services.yaml:29-39). PrometheusDeploy's judgment layer names it in Alertmanager's served_by (architecture.yaml:18-21, which names only Telegram's Bot API at planning), so the published architecture draws healthchecks.io serving Alertmanager. The Architecture repo is public, and the entry carries nothing of the operator's check.

ElasticsearchDeploy's README names the reader-password rotation path (Ruling review-A2): `bao kv put` the new value, then make the setup Job rerun by deleting it so that Argo CD recreates it. Followed as written, the path leaves Elasticsearch on the new password. It accounts for ESO's hourly refresh of the Secret (ElasticsearchDeploy chart/values.yaml:39-40). It also accounts for Argo CD not recreating a deleted Job on its own: the app auto-syncs with selfHeal false (ArgoCDDeploy releases/templates/applications.yaml:67-70, and live), and auto-sync skips a revision it has already synced (argo-cd v3.5.1 controller/appcontroller.go:2401-2403). Nothing re-applies a changed password automatically.
